transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Um... it's mostly about work. I got written up last week, so... I guess I came in because I keep getting stuck at the register. Just... doing things that don't really fit the moment. 

Like, I'll start tapping the scanner in a pattern. Or I'll just freeze with my hand hovering over the cash drawer, while the customer is just standing there waiting. So... yeah. That's why.
When you find yourself tapping the scanner in that pattern, are you doing it because you feel a strong urge to make it 'just right' or to prevent something bad from happening?

No... it's not like that. I don't... I don't think about anything bad happening. 

I just... I just tap it. I don't really know why.

Besides your hands, do you ever feel like you have to make sudden, jerky movements with your neck, shoulders, or face, or do you ever find yourself making sounds or clearing your throat when you don't need to?

Um... no. I don't think so. 

I haven't really noticed anything like that. Just... just what I already said.
During these moments when you freeze or tap the scanner, do you ever feel like you have 'lost time' or that you have no memory of what happened during those few seconds?

No... I remember it. I can see the customer standing right there. 

I just... I don't know. I'm just stuck. But I don't forget it.
Have you ever had a serious head injury, a seizure, or been diagnosed with any neurological condition like epilepsy or a brain tumor?
No... I haven't had anything like that. No head injuries or... seizures. Nothing like that.
Have friends or family mentioned that your personality has changed, or that you have become more impulsive or socially inappropriate recently?
No... nobody has said anything like that to me. I just... I'm the same as I've always been, I think. I mostly just keep to myself anyway.
Before you tap the scanner or freeze, do you feel any kind of physical sensation or 'itch' in your body that is relieved only once you perform the action?
No... I don't think so. It's not like an itch or... anything physical. I don't feel anything in my body before it happens. I just... do it.
When you are stuck at the register, does it feel like you are watching yourself from the outside or that you are somehow disconnected from your own body?
No... not like that. I'm... I'm still me. I don't feel disconnected or... like I'm watching myself. I'm just there.

Do you ever find yourself repeating words or phrases under your breath, or making any small, repetitive movements like blinking or shrugging that you might have just become so used to that you don't even notice them anymore?
No... I don't think so. I haven't noticed anything like that. Just... regular movements, I guess. Nothing out of the ordinary.
Do you often feel physical pain or discomfort in your body that doesn't seem to have a clear medical cause?
No... I don't think I do. I mean, just the usual aches from standing at the register all day, but... nothing strange. Just normal pain, I guess.
When you are not at work, do you find it difficult to switch tasks or do you get stuck in repetitive routines in your daily life at home?
No, not really. I just... I do what I need to do around the house. It's just normal stuff. I don't get stuck doing the same thing over and over. Just... regular routines.
Are you able to stop these movements if you really try to, or do you feel like your body is going to perform them regardless of your effort to stay still?

I... I don't think I can stop it. I guess... that's actually why I came in. I didn't really want to bring it up, but at the register, I just... I keep getting stuck doing things that don't fit the moment. Like... I'll start tapping the scanner in a pattern. Or I'll just freeze with my hand hovering over the cash drawer, even with a customer just standing there waiting. I try to snap out of it, but... I can't always. It... it got me written up last week.
Have you noticed any recent changes in your memory, your ability to concentrate, or how clearly you are able to think?
No... I don't think so. My memory seems fine. I just... I do my job, and I come home. I haven't noticed any changes with my thinking.
Have you ever experienced any weakness, numbness, or tingling in any part of your body that comes and goes?
No... I haven't. Nothing like that.

Does this 'getting stuck' or tapping behavior happen only when you are at the register at work, or does it ever occur when you are alone at home or in other places where there is no pressure from customers?

I... mostly just notice it at work. Like I said before, it's at the register where it's a real issue. The tapping... freezing up while people wait. That's what got me written up last week. 

If I do it at home... I don't really know. There's no one watching me there, so it doesn't matter as much. I just know it's messing up my job.

When you are at work, does this 'getting stuck' or tapping behavior happen more often when the store is busy and you feel pressured, or does it happen even when it is quiet and you have no customers waiting?

I guess... it happens both times. It doesn't seem to matter if there's a line or not. 

I just get stuck doing things that don't really fit the moment. Sometimes it's quiet and I'll just be... tapping the scanner in a pattern. But if it is busy, I'll just freeze with my hand over the cash drawer while the customer is standing right there waiting. It just... happens.

Have you ever been told by anyone, or have you ever noticed yourself, doing these same repetitive tapping or freezing behaviors while you are in a completely different environment, such as when you are at home or out shopping for yourself?
I don't know... I haven't really noticed. No one's said anything to me about it. Just... just at work.
If you were to sit down at home and focus entirely on being still, do you feel like you could stop these movements, or would your body still perform them?
I... I don't know. I haven't really tried to do that. I just... I don't really think about it when I'm at home.
When you are about to perform these movements, do you experience any kind of uncomfortable sensation or building tension in your body that is only relieved after you complete the movement?
No... I don't think so. I don't feel any... tension, or anything building up. It's not like that. It just... happens.

When you are about to start tapping or freezing, do you feel any subtle, odd, or unusual physical sensation in your muscles or limbs that makes you feel like you *must* do the movement to make it go away?
No... I don't feel anything in my muscles. Um... it's just like I said before. I don't feel like I have to do it to make anything go away. I just... I don't really notice it starting.
